the interfacial transition zones of cement mortars prepared using polynaphthalenesulfonate-based superplasticizer are characterized by a lower electrical conductivity, smaller interfacial conductance and lower porosity than those prepared with the same cement and without superplasticizer.

the electrical resistance and interfacial excess conductivity values of mortars containing relatively large dosages of PNS superplasticizer were higher and lower, respectively, compared to the corresponding values of control mortars.

the characterization of the interfacial transition zones of mortars containing relatively higher dosages of polycarboxylate superplasticizer (PNS).

, at the relatively high superplasticizer dosages used in the present work, the PNS superplasticizer is not able to improve the microstructural and electrical conductivity characteristics of Portland cement mortar, compared to the control mortars.

PNS superplasticizers are not detrimental to the microstructure of cementitious systems at relatively high dosing levels, but they do affect the interfacial transition zones in such systems, as well as the overall porosity of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PNS superplasticizer has a detrimental effect on the electrical properties and microstructure of mortars.
the interfacial transition zones (ITZ) in cementitious systems are characterized by a relatively low electrical conductivity, a low porosity and a high electrical resistance.
the electrical conductance of cementitious composites is influenced by the interfacial transition layer, which can be modeled using Bruggeman’s theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that

PNS superplasticizers can significantly reduce the electrical conductivity of mortars and that the electrical resistance of mortars is a function of both the relative conductivity and the interfacial transition zones.

the use of PNS superplasticizers at relatively high dosing levels results in a reduction of the interfacial transition zones in cement mortars, which in turn results in a decrease of their conductivity and porosity.

the interfacial transition zones in mortars containing relatively large dosages of polycarboxylate ether (PCE) superplasticizers have a lower electrical conductance and a lower porosity compared with those in mortars containing polynaphthalenesulfonate (PNS) or no superplasticizer.
